objective: Review the two merge commits that stack the Pi wiring branches (28d2b56 on release/0.3.0/feat/pi-tool-settings and eb12e30 on release/0.3.0/feat/pi-review-prompts) for merge mistakes.
scope: 28d2b56 merges release/0.3.0/feat/pi-root-wiring (e2b516b) into pi-tool-settings; eb12e30 merges pi-tool-settings into pi-review-prompts. Worktrees /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-settings and /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-prompts. Both merged without conflicts.

Check with git show --cc and git diff of each parent against the merge that no change from either side was lost or duplicated, especially in files both sides touched (docs/pi/extensions.md, docs/pi/README.md, docs/pi/configuration.md, docs/usage.md, the generated dist bundles); that statements in those docs still agree with the merged code; and that the generated dist matches the merged sources (a fresh build left both trees clean and verify passed: 2334 and 2352 pass).
constraints: Read-only; no edits and no version-control writes.

criteria.text: Each merge keeps every change of both parents, and the merged docs agree with the merged code

result:
result: One blocker. Both merges keep every change from both parents, but `docs/pi/configuration.md` is stale against the merged code in 28d2b56 and eb12e30.

changed: none (read-only)

checks:
- I did not rerun `mise run build` or `mise run verify`. The root's report is that a fresh build left both trees clean and verify passed (2334 and 2352 pass).
- `git status --short` in `/home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-settings` and `/home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-prompts` -> both clean, HEAD at 28d2b56 and eb12e30.
- Comparison of each parent's changes against the merge, over everything outside `dist/` -> no change lost or duplicated for either parent of either merge. The only differences are hunk line offsets in `docs/pi/extensions.md`.
- `git diff-tree --cc` -> only `docs/pi/extensions.md` and the two `dist/scripts/holyagent.js` bundles differ from both parents. The docs edits sit in disjoint hunks and the bundles are regenerated output.
- `packages/integrations/pi/dist/extensions/holyagent.js` and `src/extension.ts` are byte-identical (same blob) across e2b516b, 28d2b56 and eb12e30. The merged bundles contain the new `ModelId` pattern with `@+` and both sides' code.

blockers:
- `docs/pi/configuration.md` line 43 says the `pi.routes.<row>.model` pattern is `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]{0,127}$`, with "`.` `_` `:` `/` `-`". The merged `packages/runtime/src/config/schema.ts:51` is `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/@+-]{0,127}$`.
- The cause is that the settings side added that doc line and the root-wiring side widened the charset, so git saw no conflict. `docs/pi/providers.md` was updated for `@` and `+`, but this file was not.
- Fix: update the pattern and the prose in `configuration.md` line 43 to include `@` and `+`.

questions: none

notes:
- Code-review findings on the root-wiring commits themselves are outside the merge question. I did not verify them against running code, and I rate all of them optional:
  - `INVISIBLES` strips ZWJ, ZWNJ and VS16, which are legitimate in emoji and Persian or Indic text.
  - `taken.excluded` only grows within a session, which the docs state on purpose.
  - `homeNotice` can be shown again after each collection once delivered.
  - The user-config subprocess now runs on every collection.
  - `Fiber.join(userRead)` can turn a defect in the user read into a failed collection.
  - `joinNotices` dedupes by substring.
  - The second review raised a possible mismatch when only a project turns `pi.enable` off: the exclusions are enforced in `tool_call`, but Pi's active tools are not restricted. The docs describe this behaviour for the project-off case.
  - `ModelId` now accepts `@` and `+`.

evidence:
- Each merge keeps every change of both parents, and the merged docs agree with the merged code: Merge preservation holds for both merges, using `git diff <merge-base> <parent>` against `git diff <other-parent> <merge>`, empty apart from line offsets. The docs-versus-code check fails on `docs/pi/configuration.md:43`, whose model-id pattern lacks `@` and `+` in both merges.
- review-findings: the blocker above; two `/code-review medium` runs (74d9379...28d2b56 and 95a9099...eb12e30) returned only the optional root-wiring findings listed in notes.
